subject: Archimedes Dedicated: floor, ladder, and on-ramp options
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@archimedes.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — our expected baseline and ask

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looked great. We’re starting to sketch out what a Dedicated contract would look like for Archimedes. High level: our initial ML workload will be a mix of streaming chat (low-latency) and batch embeddings for nightly indexing.

Rough demand profile (estimates):
- Weekday peak concurrency: ~700 concurrent tokens/sec (chat + short contexts)
- Nightly batch window: 2–3 hours, sustained high throughput for embeddings
- Growth: expect ~3x over 6–9 months if initial tests go well

Can you send a few concrete commit options (cluster sizes, minimum GPU floors, suggested ramp cadence, and what burst capacity looks like) so our procurement team has something to evaluate? We also need a short exec summary for procurement and a packet we can share with our infra/security folks (SOC2/VPC notes).

Thanks — looping in Kate (procurement).

Samir
Archimedes AI

Attachments: product_requirements_v1.pdf (referenced)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@archimedes.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — our expected baseline and ask

Samir — really appreciate the clarity. See below three pragmatic commit options built to match the workload mix you described. I’ve attached a one-page summary (proposed_commitment_tiers.pdf) and flagged the items we need from you to finalize pricing.

Executive summary (short):
- Option A — Trial floor (conservative): 12 active A100-equivalent GPUs minimum. 30-day canary, burst to +20 GPUs for peak. Best for proof-of-value with limited commitment.
- Option B — Growth ladder (recommended): 40 min GPUs with scheduled ramp windows (month 1: 10 baseline active, month 3: 25, month 6: 40). Includes 15% burst capacity and pre-warmed KV cache for chat workloads.
- Option C — Production floor (SLA-backed): 100 min GPUs with guaranteed throughput and reserved lanes for low-latency chat. Includes dedicated autoscale lanes and priority routing.

Technical notes (high level):
- GPU mix: primarily A100 / H100 class depending on quantization; we’ll recommend quantized 8-bit variants for embed-heavy batch jobs.
- Batching & latency controls: runtime will limit batch size for short-context chat and allow larger batches for embeddings to control p99 latency.
- Warm-up: recommended 48–72 hour warm-up for KV cache before full cutover to reduce early latency spikes.

Questions we need from Archimedes to firm the proposal:
1) Typical average sequence length for chat (tokens) and batch embedding sizes.
2) Expected daily queries and percent during the nightly batch window.
3) Any required blackout windows for deployment or maintenance.

Next steps: if you can confirm model mix + expected concurrency numbers we’ll produce a priced proposal and an implementation timeline (including canary, stage ramp, GA).

Attachments: proposed_commitment_tiers.pdf (1-page summary)

Thanks,
Ava Chen

Ava / Samir — quick technical addendum to the options above (added a short workbook attached with model footprints):

Operational considerations:
- GPU sizing: when we say "12 A100-equivalent" that maps to either 6x A100-80GB (multi-GPU packing) or 12x smaller cards depending on what you prefer for fault isolation. We recommend a minimum of 2 replicas per working set for redundancy.
- Minimum lanes vs. autoscale: the "min GPUs" is a billing floor and a warm pool; autoscale can add transient GPUs for short spikes, but steady-state should be covered by the committed floor to keep queueing minimal.
- Burst model: guaranteed +15% burst with 10-minute preempt window for non-critical batch. For low-latency traffic we hold reserved lanes that cannot be preempted.
- Warm-up and cache priming: use a small synthetic traffic generator during the 48–72 hour warm-up to populate KV cache and embeddings indexes.

Suggested on-ramp (technical cadence):
- Week 0–4: Canary — 10 active GPUs, traffic mirroring at 10% of production.
- Month 2–3: Mid-stage — 25 active GPUs with index re-ingestion in off-peak window.
- Month 6: Full production — 40 active GPUs (Option B) or more based on telemetry.

I’ve attached a short workbook with model mix recommended allocations (archimedes_onramp_model_mix.xlsx). If you want, we can run an infra sizing session with your MLEs to map exact sLOs to GPU counts.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Ava & Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/ops: 

- We’re leaning toward Option B (Growth ladder) but we will need a 6-month minimum committed floor for contract language. Can you provide an SLA-backed variant that pins the month-6 floor (40 GPUs) with monthly ramp triggers?
- For SOC2/VPC: please include a one-page security appendix describing network isolation, KMS integration, and audit log access.
- Pricing ask: procurement needs a monthly breakdown that shows committed floor vs. burst overage pricing.

Operational note: our infra lead expects the baseline for chat to run at roughly 120 GPU-equivalent concurrent throughput (this is a conservative internal mapping). We can run a sizing workshop next week if you think that will help lock the model mix.

Kate (procurement) — feel free to add any procurement-specific constraints.

Samir
